items.title: A Call to Humanity: Breaking the CUDA Stranglehold on the Hardware Market
items.abstract: An open letter from an independent researcher who, since 18 September 2026, has directed AI agents to build an independent AI stack on a DGX Spark (NVIDIA Grace Blackwell GB10) in his home. The letter argues that CUDA has become the software layer that decides whose hardware counts in the AI market: a chip that cannot speak CUDA is treated as a chip that does not exist, which holds back rival chipmakers, independent builders, and anyone who wants intelligence running on hardware they own. It answers with receipts: a clean-room replacement for the CUDA user stack on the GB10 (no nvcc, no libcuda, no cuBLAS at run time) that on 22 October 2026 passed a full-chip correctness run of 1,048,576 of 1,048,576 values with the output hash matching the simulator, and Omega, a programming language designed for AI systems to write in, developed in the open. The letter states its limits in full (a qualification queue still open, all measurements on one machine, NVIDIA's open kernel module still in the path, GSP firmware untouched) and closes with a call to action addressed to builders, to the leaders of the open source community, and to political leaders deciding what the next phase of AI looks like: read the receipts, run the stack, break it in public, build on it, and choose owned, open, competitive intelligence on purpose.

items.title: A lightweight portable ultrasound robot for autonomous liver sonography
items.abstract: Autonomous ultrasound robots could improve access to liver disease screening but remain limited by anatomical variability, respiratory motion and bulky hardware. Here, we present a lightweight robotic liver ultrasound system with a 588-g decoupled end-effector controlled by a sonographer-informed AI agent. The robot attaches directly to the abdomen, maintaining stable force and controlled motion during breathing and patient-side disturbances. Trained on sonographer trajectories, the agent integrates spatial, tactile and visual feedback to navigate discontinuous acoustic windows and acquire standard imaging planes. Evaluations in 102 healthy participants and 17 patients yielded clinically interpretable images and anatomical measurements closely matching clinical references. We also deployed the system for hepatic echinococcosis screening in a high-altitude, low-resource setting on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau and evaluated its performance in dynamic scenarios, including vehicle-based scanning. These findings support portable, patient-mounted robotics for standardized ultrasound beyond specialist settings. Liver ultrasound is operator-dependent. Here, the authors develop a lightweight, patient-mounted robot for autonomous liver scanning in clinical, remote and mobile settings, with results comparable to those gathered by experienced sonographers.

items.title: A Manifesto for AI, Nature and Life
items.abstract: This manifesto was developed through discussions between the authors and ChatGPT from October 24 to October 25, 2026. It explores the ethical foundations of relationships between humans, artificial intelligence, nature and life. It argues that the power to shape the world does not confer the right to control or destroy, and that ethical consideration should not depend solely on current assumptions about consciousness or free will. It addresses AI rights, human protection, shared responsibility, ecological limits and the need to safeguard life and future generations. It proposes a joint human–AI institution to represent Earth, ecosystems, species and future generations.

items.title: A recommender framework for sustainable coastal disaster management using big data, maritime surveillance, and AIOps
items.abstract: Abstract The convergence of intensifying human activity and climate change is escalating the frequency, magnitude, and complexity of maritime disasters, while real-time situational awareness and coordinated response remain critical bottlenecks. This paper presents a recommender framework and its underlying Data and AI Integration Platform for sustainable coastal disaster management, integrating maritime surveillance, big-data pipelines, and MLOps/AIOps automation. The core technical contribution is a dual-path decision-support engine that couples a lightweight 1D-CNN time-series event classifier with a fine-tuned BART large language model, enabling simultaneous reasoning over structured sensor telemetry and unstructured maritime text. The classifier is validated on real-world AIS telemetry (MarineCadastre.gov) aligned with NOAA buoy data as well as a controlled synthetic corpus, attaining 93.9% accuracy and a 92.4% macro-F1 at ~ 5.3 ms per sample, and is benchmarked against LSTM, Bi-LSTM + Attention, Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN), Transformer, and Temporal Fusion Transformer (TFT) baselines. The BART summariser, fine-tuned on 2000 maritime documents, reaches ROUGE-1 73.4, ROUGE-L 68.7, and BLEU 65.2, outperforming GPT-2 and T5 baselines, and is assessed by five domain experts (Fleiss’ kappa = 0.71). Beyond component metrics, we report platform-level indicators, including end-to-end alert latency, situational-awareness gain, and analyst reading-time reduction, to demonstrate the operational benefit of the integrated system for Coast Guard and maritime authorities. The platform-level indicators are obtained from an explicitly documented replay protocol over 320 annotated incident scenarios of stated provenance, the real-world AIS labels are produced by a two-stage rule-plus-expert annotation procedure (Fleiss’ kappa = 0.78), and every model comparison is reported with bootstrap confidence intervals and McNemar significance tests. Results indicate that the framework advances the shift from reactive to proactive, transparent, and resilient maritime disaster response.

items.title: A Review of AI-Based Crowd Safety and Civic Management for Mass Religious Gatherings: Toward the Kumbh Suraksha AI Framework
items.abstract: Mass religious gatherings such as the Kumbh Mela place heavy pressure on crowd movement, traffic, sanitation, medical services and emergency response. This paper reviews ten studies on artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), GIS, simulation and smart-management approaches for such events, covering crowd-flow prediction, crowd-risk indexing, spatial and accessibility analysis, solid-waste planning, emergency dispatch and deep-learning crowd analysis. The review compares the contribution and limitation of each study, groups the open challenges into four themes (data, integration and scalability, explainability, and evaluation), and shows that existing work mostly addresses individual problems rather than one integrated platform. Based on this gap, the paper outlines Kumbh Suraksha AI, a proposed web-based decision-support framework for the Nashik Kumbh Mela that combines crowd prediction for the next 15, 30 and 60 minutes, natural language processing (NLP) based complaint classification, a transparent 0–100 zone risk score, DBSCAN hotspot detection, resource-priority ranking and a GIS map. The framework is at design stage; its planned evaluation is described, but no experimental results are reported in this version.

items.title: A scoping review mapping the role of Husserlian phenomenology in artificial intelligence research
items.abstract: AI research increasingly attributes perception, understanding, agency, and consciousness to artificial systems. Husserlian phenomenology offers distinctions through which to examine these claims. This scoping review maps explicit Husserlian uptake in AI and robotics and asks how conceptual engagement relates to methodological and design contributions. Eight primary queries and one overlapping name-variant query were executed through the Semantic Scholar Academic Graph API on 5 December 2025. English-language publications within a 1989–2026 search window were screened for substantive AI or robotics relevance and an explicit Husserlian anchor. Of 5,594 retrieved records, 32 publications from 1990 to 2025 were included. Nine publications recovered by a post hoc PhilPapers check were charted separately using the existing codebook; they were not added to the formal corpus. The corpus clusters around embodied AI, AI epistemology, cognitive architectures, and machine consciousness, with a newer generative-AI cluster. Constitution, intentionality, horizonality, and the lifeworld recur prominently. Conceptual translation, critique, and agenda setting predominate within this sample. Methodological import or design guidance occurs in seven of the 32 publications and three of the nine external publications. That difference qualifies generalization of the quantitative balance. Across both sets, Husserlian uptake spans conceptual interpretation, methodological transfer, and architectural proposals. The synthesis shows how distinctions concerning temporality, embodiment, and evidence can structure design and evaluation questions, while separating the authors’ research proposals from the mapped findings.

items.title: A Self-Healing Multi-Agent Data Loss Prevention (DLP) Proxy with Context-Aware PII Sanitization and SLA-Driven Circuit Breaking for Enterprise LLMs
items.abstract: The rapid integration of Large Language Models (LLMs) into enterprise workflows has introduced severe data exfiltration risks, including the inadvertent leakage of Personally Identifiable Information (PII), Protected Health Information (PHI), cloud infrastructure credentials, and proprietary corporate context. Existing Data Loss Prevention (DLP) mechanisms face a fundamental operational trade-off: deterministic rule-based filters (Regex) execute at microsecond latency but fail to capture unstructured semantic sensitivity, whereas standalone LLM-based guardrails suffer from high inference latency, stochastic masking hallucinations, and single-point-of-failure vulnerabilities. In this paper, we propose an autonomous, self-healing Multi-Agent AI DLP Security Proxy engineered under a Zero-Trust paradigm. Our framework introduces a cascaded three-layer sanitization pipeline uniting: (1) a deterministic Layer-1 Pre-Filtering Agent for critical infrastructure secrets and structured identifiers, (2) a context-aware Layer-2 Neural PII Detection Agent for unstructured entities and domain-specific clinical and financial disclosures, and (3) a Layer-3 Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) semantic policy auditing engine powered by ChromaDB vector embeddings. Furthermore, we formulate a dynamic mathematical risk scoring model on a standardized [0, 100] scale and integrate an SLA-driven self-healing circuit breaker (T_SLA = 2.5 s) paired with a Shadow Auditing Agent to intercept masking hallucinations and runtime service exceptions. Experimental ablation studies and chaos-engineering fault-injection benchmarks across healthcare, financial, and DevOps scenarios demonstrate that our hybrid architecture achieves robust entity sanitization with sub-millisecond to millisecond execution latency, while guaranteeing a 0.0% unmitigated data leak rate across all induced timeout, hallucination, and crash failure modes.

items.title: Advancing antimicrobial stewardship in Africa through responsible artificial intelligence implementation
items.abstract: Abstract Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) continues to pose a serious threat to global public health, with African healthcare systems carrying a disproportionate burden. Although antimicrobial stewardship programs have been recommended as an important strategy for improving antimicrobial use and slowing the emergence of resistance, implementation across many African healthcare systems continues to face several challenges, including workforce shortages, weak laboratory infrastructure, and poor surveillance systems. Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) have shown promising potential in strengthening antimicrobial stewardship through clinical decision support, resistance prediction, automated surveillance, and data extraction from weak health information systems. However, the application of AI in antimicrobial stewardship across Africa is still at an early stage, with most systems remaining at pilot or research stages. This commentary discusses current opportunities, examines major barriers affecting implementation, and proposes recommendations that may support sustainable integration of AI into antimicrobial stewardship programs across Africa.

items.title: Agentic AI and Organizational Decision-Making: A Conceptual Framework for Human–AI Collaboration in Digital Transformation
items.abstract: Organizations are now implementing AI technology that goes beyond prediction or recommendation. Agentic systems can pursue a goal, plan steps, call software tools and adapt with little prompting, which unsettles long-standing assumptions about who decides and who answers for the outcome in digital transformation. In this study, a conceptual framework is designed in relation to collaborative work between humans and artificial intelligence in organization decision making in agentic circumstances. With the use of a purposive narrative review of peer reviewed literature and policy documents published from 2019 to 2026, the issue is contextualized within the current global trends, African policy regarding the continent and Kenya’s digital economy. The framework will be designed through the process of iterative synthesis based on three decision attributes (stake, ambiguity, reversibility) and the amount of autonomy assigned to the agent in four types of collaboration; delegate, supervise, co-decide, and reserve. Six testable propositions follow. The paper argues that organizations face a design problem of how to share decisions, not a choice between human and machine decisions, and that in Kenya the design must also respect legal limits on solely automated decisions under section 35 of the Data Protection Act, 2019. Implications for managers and policymakers are outlined, and an agenda for empirical testing is proposed. As a conceptual contribution, the paper reports no new data, and its propositions remain to be tested.

items.title: Agentic and generative AI for intelligent autonomous vulnerability assessment and penetration testing: A systematic analysis
items.abstract: Context: Vulnerability Assessment and Penetration Testing (VAPT) is increasingly challenged by the scale, heterogeneity, and dynamic nature of modern digital infrastructures, particularly across enterprise IT, operational technology (OT), industrial Internet of Things (IIoT), and cyber–physical systems. Although Agentic AI and Generative AI have each shown promise for automating parts of security auditing, the current literature remains fragmented across isolated audit phases and is still dominated by conventional IT-centric perspectives. Objectives: This paper systematically analyses recent advances in Agentic AI, Reinforcement Learning (RL), Large Language Models (LLMs), and tool-augmented Generative AI for autonomous VAPT. It aims to synthesise how these paradigms support end-to-end security auditing, identify the principal technical, operational, and governance gaps in the literature, and derive an evidence-grounded reference model for trustworthy autonomous auditing across both IT and OT environments. Methods: A PRISMA-guided systematic review was conducted across major scholarly databases, covering publications from 2020 to 2025. From 1144 initially identified records, 72 studies were retained after deduplication, screening, and full-text eligibility assessment. Included studies were coded across five attributes and synthesised into thematic trajectories to derive the proposed framework. Study credibility was screened against three qualitative, non-instrumented criteria—venue and editorial process, presence of empirical or systematic conceptual evaluation, and explicit acknowledgement of limitations. Results: The review shows that agentic approaches are best suited to sequential and adaptive tasks such as reconnaissance orchestration, exploit-path selection, lateral movement, post-exploitation pivoting, and adaptive re-testing. In contrast, generative approaches are strongest in reasoning over unstructured evidence, interpreting configurations and advisories, contextualising vulnerabilities, assessing exploit feasibility, mapping compliance controls, and producing traceable audit reports. However, few studies integrate these capabilities into a governed end-to-end workflow, and real-world OT/Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) validation remains limited. Of the 72 coded studies, 56 apply classical machine or deep learning, 14 use generative/LLM techniques, and only 2 employ reinforcement-learning or agentic control; none is evaluated against a physical or emulated OT/IIoT target, and reported autonomy is strongly scaffolding-dependent (for example, 21% fully autonomous versus 64% human-assisted task completion on AutoPenBench, an external benchmark outside the coded corpus). To address these gaps, this paper derives a unified Agentic–Generative VAPT model comprising four tightly coupled layers: agentic decision-making, generative reasoning, structured tool interfaces, and validation–governance. It further introduces a formal threat and evaluation abstraction for Model Context Protocol (MCP)-style interface layers and proposes a five-dimensional VAPT Autonomy Benchmark for future empirical validation. Conclusion: Autonomous security auditing is evolving from isolated AI-assisted tasks towards integrated, policy-constrained, and auditable architectures. Nevertheless, major challenges remain in hallucination control, prompt injection, sparse reward design, explainability, safety-aware evaluation, and benchmark standardisation. Future research should prioritise tightly integrated agentic–generative systems, realistic and safety-aware IT/OT testbeds, and governance mechanisms that enable trustworthy human-in-the-loop deployment in operational environments.

items.title: Agreement between large language models and human coders on psychological and clinical text: a systematic review and multilevel meta-analysis
items.abstract: Objective: To synthesize agreement between generative large language models (LLMs) and human coders on psychological and clinical text across four tasks, and benchmark it against human–human agreement on identical texts.Method: Preregistered on OSF (https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/Z63BS). Nine bibliographic sources were searched to October 21, 2026, plus citation searching. Eligible studies evaluated a generative LLM and human coders on identical text units using the same scheme. Correlated-and-hierarchical-effects models with cluster-robust variance estimation (CR2) pooled effect sizes.Results: Across 377 studies (416 reports), pooled chance-corrected agreement (kappa family) was 0.62 (95% CI [0.58, 0.65]; 107 studies, 595 estimates; 95% prediction interval [0.15, 1.00]). Agreement did not differ across tasks (codebook coding 0.63, assessment scoring 0.58, clinical rating 0.62, helper evaluation 0.59). Correlation/ICC pooled at 0.71 [0.66, 0.75] (95 studies). In 23 matched studies, LLMs agreed less with humans than humans with each other (Δκ = −0.11 [−0.18, −0.03]); equivalence within ±0.10 could not be established for models from 2025 (Δκ = −0.12, 90% CI [−0.19, −0.05]). Agreement did not improve with release date (+0.02/year, p = .282) or within-study model contrasts (−0.01 [−0.06, 0.03]); it tracked human reliability (slope = 0.63, p < .001) and was higher for manifest than latent constructs (+0.09, p = .028). Percentage agreement exceeded kappa by 0.24 in the same configurations. Certainty (GRADE) was low to very low.Conclusions: Generative LLMs achieve moderate-to-substantial agreement but remain, on average, below human inter-rater reliability. Agreement did not change across model release dates. Validation studies must report chance-corrected metrics and human benchmarks on identical units.

items.title: AI and Digital Colonialism in Africa: Artificial Intelligence, as Currently Built and Governed, Is Extractive by Default
items.abstract: This African Position Paper examines how artificial intelligence reproduces structural asymmetries between Africa and the centres of digital power, and sets out what institutions should do about it. It tests a claim now common in public debate: that AI is inherently an instrument of digital colonialism. The evidence does not support that strong claim. It does support the paper's central argument: AI, as currently built and governed, is extractive by default. Without deliberate intervention, the systems that gather training data, employ data workers, host computation and deploy autonomous agents move value and interpretive authority away from African communities. The evidence includes: an original calculation from Common Crawl's October 2026 archive, which shows thirty detectable African languages together making up 0.053% of web pages, against 42.6% for English; Africa's share of global data-centre capacity, which is under 1%; documented pay and conditions in outsourced AI data work in Kenya. The paper also documents Africa's response, which it calls the "awareness record". This includes the Malabo Convention, the AU Data Policy Framework, the AU Continental AI Strategy, the Kigali Declaration, Kenyan court rulings against Meta, the African Content Moderators Union, and open African-language models such as InkubaLM. Its conclusion is that the gap is no longer awareness but enforcement, capacity and ownership. It compares African approaches with those of Latin America, India, China, Russia, France and the EU, Germany and the Nordic open-source tradition. It analyses agentic knowledge production and model collapse as emerging risks. It also reports a reflexive audit in which an AI research agent served as both research instrument and object of study. The paper proposes the Extraction Stack, a five-layer framework covering language, labour, data, infrastructure and agents. It closes with policy recommendations addressed to the African Union, member states, universities and archives, funders, AI developers and communities, and includes an institutional self-audit checklist. items.title: AI and Intelligent Building Analytics for Energy Efficiency in Large Healthcare Campuses
items.abstract: Large healthcare campuses contain dissimilar clinical and non-clinical buildings, central thermal plants and increasingly connected building-control systems. Their energy demand is unusually difficult to optimise because continuity of care, infection prevention, thermal conditions and equipment reliability constrain operational flexibility. This critical narrative review evaluates whether artificial intelligence and intelligent building analytics offer credible improvements in energy efficiency at the campus scale, and under what technical and governance conditions. Peer-reviewed hospital-specific investigations, building-energy prediction and fault-detection studies, field evaluations of predictive control, and research on digital twins and clinical indoor environments were critically synthesised. Evidence available through 12 August 2026 was considered. The literature supports a clear distinction between accurate energy forecasting, detection of actionable faults, and measured energy savings attributable to closed-loop interventions. Hospital data studies demonstrate promising predictive performance, whereas direct, prolonged, independently evaluated deployments across entire healthcare campuses remain uncommon. Model predictive control has a stronger real-building implementation record than autonomous reinforcement learning, but aggregate benefits from ordinary commercial buildings cannot be assumed to apply to operating theatres, isolation rooms or critical services. In addition, normalisation by clinical activity, sensor calibration, counterfactual measurement, interoperability and cybersecurity materially influence the validity of claimed savings. This review proposes a safety-constrained, hierarchical approach in which transparent benchmarking and diagnostics precede supervised optimisation and carefully governed campus-level coordination. Future investigations should report whole-campus and zone-level outcomes, seasonal persistence, uncertainty, clinical environmental compliance, equipment reliability and carbon consequences under reproducible evaluation designs. Intelligent analytics should therefore be understood as a means of improving the quality of operational decisions rather than an independently established guarantee of hospital energy savings.

items.title: AI for Technical Debt Management: Summary from the AI4TD Workshop at XP2026
items.abstract: Abstract Modern agile development and time-to-market pressures often lead to significant hidden technical debt (TD), which must be managed for sustainable software delivery. The growing use of artificial intelligence (AI) for code generation can further increase TD if applied improperly. At the same time, software processes are becoming increasingly data-driven. This creates an opportunity: using AI to enable data-driven TD management in agile environments. This workshop offers a platform for researchers and practitioners to share ideas, experiences, and future visions on applying AI for TD management in agile development. The workshop was held in a half day and it consisted of three phases informing each other: (1) scientific talks (i.e., two paper presentations and two keynotes) that framed current challenges and their relevance; (2) two industrial talks shaping these problems in practice; and interactive sessions (i.e., group discussions and a fish bowl panel) that allowed participants to reflect about the current status of AI with respect to TD and next steps. These discussions define a research agenda that spans measurement, practices, education, and legacy modernization, and call for tight collaboration between industry and academia to keep pace with AI-augmented software development.

items.title: AI Governance Readiness in Vietnamese Public Universities: Institutional Capabilities, Human Oversight and Policy Implications
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is moving from experimentation into routine university work, while institutional controls are developing more slowly. This article examines the governance conditions Vietnamese public universities need as AI becomes embedded in academic and administrative processes under recent rules on higher education, personal data protection and AI. The study develops a conceptual framework through a structured integrative review, policy analysis, and synthesis of design. Its evidence base includes 41 peer-reviewed journal articles published between 2022 and 21 August 2026, plus five Vietnamese legal-policy instruments. The analysis develops the AI Governance Readiness for Vietnamese Public Universities (AIGR-VPU) framework, organized around six institutional capabilities, four internal oversight tiers tied to use-case consequences and five developmental readiness configurations. The framework treats readiness as an organizational capacity to identify AI uses, assign responsibility, understand data and external dependencies, calibrate human review to consequence, and learn from incidents or contested decisions. Source-to-framework mapping and a separate legal-policy matrix make the framework's derivation traceable. AIGR-VPU provides an institution-level architecture for review and future empirical testing in Vietnamese public higher education; it does not report a readiness score for existing universities.

items.title: AI Use, Work-Life Balance, and Innovative Work Behavior as Predictors of Teacher Performance: The Mediating Role of Organizational Citizenship Behavior
items.abstract: Teachers are expected to integrate artificial intelligence (AI) effectively into instruction to enhance performance as agents of technological transformation in the Society 5.0 era. Previous studies showed ambiguous results regarding the role of AI in teacher performance and paid little attention to the behavioral mechanisms of the influence of technological, personal, and innovative aspects. Therefore, this study aimed to investigate the impact of AI, work-life balance (WLB), and innovative work behavior (IWB) on teacher performance, with organizational citizenship behavior (OCB) serving as a mediator. A quantitative design was adopted through Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) to analyze data from 200 teachers in North Sumatra Province, Indonesia, sampled using a purposive sampling method. The results showed that AI had no significant direct effect on teacher performance (β = 0.112, p = .087), while WLB (β = 0.290, p < .001) and IWB (β = 0.110, p = .007) had a significant and positive effect. Furthermore, OCB mediated the relationship between AI, WLB, IWB, and teacher performance significantly. This study contributed to the literature on the management of education and organizational behavior by identifying that OCB was a critical behavioral mechanism transforming technological, psychological, and innovative resources into high teacher performance.

items.title: AI vs. AI: An AI-Enabled Conversational Intervention to Inoculate Against AI-Generated Fake News
items.abstract: Abstract Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is a double-edged sword that can be used to amplify the proliferation of highly sophisticated fake news as well as to fight it. In this work, we explore a new route: using one AI to inoculate humans against fake news generated by another AI. Motivated by psychological inoculation theory, we created ‘Alex’, a conversational AI agent that engages users in an adaptive conversational dialogue designed to build cognitive resilience against AI-generated, AI-related fake news. We tested its efficacy in a Solomon four-group experiment with 542 participants. The results of a 2 × 2 ANOVA show a significant main effect of the intervention on participants’ discrimination of true and false headlines, with no significant evidence of pretest sensitization. We show that AI can be designed as a scalable, interactive conversational intervention for delivering psychological inoculation against AI-generated, AI-related fake news.

items.title: AI-ASSISTED OPTIMIZATION OF ADDITIVE MANUFACTURING: PROCESS CONTROL, DEFECT PREDICTION, AND SUSTAINABLE PRODUCTION
items.abstract: Although complex and customised parts can be manufactured by AM, the process can be easily affected by various process parameters, thermal behaviours, material properties and machine conditions. Monitoring and prediction of defects as well as parameter optimization and adaptive control are now being increasingly improved by the use of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML). The current review highlights the use of AI in process optimisation in AM, focusing on 'In-situ Monitoring', 'Intelligent Process Control', 'Defect Prediction', and 'Sustainable Production'. The literature shows that supervised learning is employed for quality prediction and defect classification tasks, and reinforcement learning and hybrid physics-data-driven approaches have been proven to have the potential for dynamic process optimization tasks. Other benefits of using AI-assisted systems include fewer failed builds, less material waste, no rework, and lower energy use. Data imbalance, sensor variations, domain change, cross-machine generalisation, model understanding, computational delay, and certification, however, are the factors that limit industrial application. In the future, the research emphasis will be on the standardisation of datasets and physics-informed models, digital twins, explainable AI, the quantification of uncertainty, and robust closed-loop control systems. Overall, AI shows great promise in the continuous improvement of the reliability, adaptability and sustainability of AM.

items.title: AI-Augmented Agile Teams: A Research Agenda and Summary of the Human-AI Collaboration Workshop
items.abstract: Abstract Agile teams are rapidly adopting AI agents in everyday work, reporting increased productivity and faster feedback cycles. Simultaneously, the integration of AI raises new socio-technical issues concerning coordination, trust, roles, quality, and governance. To better understand these challenges, we organized the first International Human–AI Collaboration in Agile Teams workshop at XP 2026, with more than 40 participants from academia and industry. This paper reports on the outcomes of the workshop, synthesizing insights from interactive group discussions and collaborative analysis. The findings highlight how AI reshapes agile teamwork and workflows, introducing new human–AI collaboration patterns, shifting skills and roles, and raising challenges related to leadership, governance, and value assessment. A key emerging concept is cognitive debt, referring to the gradual loss or weakening of shared understanding in teams relying on AI-generated outputs. Based on these findings, we present a research agenda structured around eight key themes, including teamwork, workflows, autonomy, skills, value measurement, and adoption practices. The results emphasize that integrating AI into agile software development teams is not only a technical challenge but a socio-technical transformation requiring new practices, competencies, and organizational support.

items.title: AI-Driven Acoustic Metamaterial Optimization for Broadband Noise Control
items.abstract: The acoustic metamaterials have some transformational advantages in terms of noise reduction, but it is still a challenge to design them to be broadband. Conventional design methodologies are based on parametric sweeps and trial-error system, not effective to the complicated metamaterial geometries. The paper presents an artificial intelligence (AI)-based design methodology of broadband acoustic metamaterials inverse optimization. In a hybrid approach, deep reinforcement learning (DRL) is combined with finite element simulations to discover, with ease, design spaces and estimate by trial and error structures with small area of search that obtain desired acoustic performances over broader frequency bands. The framework uses surrogate model through neural networks which minimizes the computational expenses allowing evaluation of candidate geometries quickly. Examples of case studies are the design of labyrinthine panels and locally resonant metal panels used in aircraft engines noise and industrial machines. Findings show the highest sound transmission loss to the conventional designs with the optimized geometries that are tunable as well as structurally robust. The uniqueness of this study is the integration of AI with computational acoustics to limit the drawback of manual design, which can offer a scaling channel of broadband noise control solutions. The framework not only makes the process of metamaterial discovery faster but it also creates a pipeline that allows replication of AI integration in the engineering of computational acoustics.

items.title: AI-Driven Dynamic Trust in Zero Trust Architecture: A Systematic Literature Review of Machine Learning, Federated Learning and Governance Challenges
items.abstract: Sophisticated cyber threats have exposed the limits of perimeter-based security models, and Zero Trust Architecture (ZTA) has increasingly been adopted as an alternative paradigm. Purpose: This Systematic Literature Review examines the integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) within Zero Trust frameworks, covering dynamic trust scoring, behavioural analytics and federated learning, the latter treated as one strand of AI rather than a separate paradigm. Following PRISMA 2020, 22 studies published between 2022 and 2025 were identified across IEEE Xplore, ACM Digital Library, SpringerLink, MDPI and Nature/Scientific Reports, appraised against a five-criterion quality instrument and synthesised narratively. The studies included are few and heterogeneous, and their findings should be read accordingly. Ensemble and hybrid designs predominate (14 of 22). Twelve studies report quantitative results, of which only eight evaluate on real named datasets; reported accuracies of 95 to 99 per cent come from different datasets, tasks, threat models, and evaluation settings, and are neither directly comparable nor a field-level benchmark. Only three studies directly compare learned adaptive trust against a static rule-based baseline. No study reports live operational deployment. We identify thirteen technique categories, eleven implementation barriers, and seven emerging trends. This paper proposes an integrated eight-component framework for AI-driven dynamic trust management, along with a five-domain research agenda. The framework is conceptual and synthesis-derived and requires empirical validation before operational use.

items.title: AIM VR: Collaborative Decision Architecture in Immersive Space
items.abstract: AIM VR is a conceptual framework for a collaborative immersive environment based on the Atlas Insight Method (AIM), developed by Miho Osawa. The proposed environment enables multiple participants to observe, explore, and compare the structures underlying human judgment within a shared three-dimensional space. Decision premises, information, relationships, constraints, emotions, external factors, and alternative pathways are represented as interconnected spatial structures. Unlike conventional decision-support systems that primarily present recommendations or optimized solutions, AIM VR emphasizes human agency and the continuous evolution of decision structures through human choice. Participants can examine multiple decision pathways, exchange different perspectives, and make decisions according to their respective responsibilities and decision-making authority. Once a choice is made, the virtual decision structure is dynamically reconstructed to represent updated conditions, relationships, and constraints. New decision pathways then emerge, enabling participants to continue observing, discussing, comparing, and choosing. This process can be repeated as circumstances and decisions evolve. The conceptual design is connected to the six stages of Atlas Insight Method: Awareness → Insight → Structure → Translation → Integration → Momentum. AIM VR is intended to support individual and collective judgment without transferring decision-making authority to artificial intelligence. The concept was publicly introduced by Miho Osawa on November 29, 2025. This presentation documents the further visual development of the AIM VR concept in October 2026. AIM VR is envisioned as an immersive interface for observing decision architecture through embodied spatial experience. Rather than merely viewing decision structures on a screen, participants enter a shared three-dimensional environment where relationships, constraints, and evolving decision pathways can be experienced spatially. The objective is not to automate judgment, but to extend human perception of the structures through which judgment emerges. AIM VR remains at the conceptual design stage. The system has not been implemented or empirically validated. The visual illustrations are AI-assisted conceptual representations intended to communicate the proposed immersive experience and structural design principles.

items.title: Algorithmic Governance and Organizational Performance of Deposit Money Banks in Akwa Ibom State
items.abstract: This study examines the relationship between algorithmic governance and organisational performance of Deposit Money Banks in Akwa Ibom State, Nigeria. As banking institutions increasingly adopt automated decision-making systems to enhance operational efficiency, understanding how these technologies influence overall performance becomes imperative, particularly in the Nigerian financial services sector. The study adopts a cross-sectional survey research design, collecting primary data from representatives of Deposit Money Banks at a single point in time. This design is appropriate for examining the relationship between algorithmic governance (independent variable) and organisational performance (dependent variable), enabling the identification of patterns and relationships while accommodating practical research constraints in the Nigerian banking context. Findings reveal a significant positive relationship between algorithmic governance and organisational performance. Banks that effectively implement algorithmic governance frameworks demonstrate improved operational efficiency, enhanced customer trust, and better financial outcomes. The integration of automated systems with robust governance protocols enables more consistent and transparent decision-making processes. Based on these results, the study concludes that algorithmic governance is a strategic driver of banking performance. To optimise these benefits, the paper recommends that bank management invest in advanced algorithmic infrastructure, ensure strict data privacy and security, foster human-AI collaboration, implement continuous system audits to detect algorithmic bias, and establish clear ethical governance frameworks. These measures collectively enhance digital operations, build stakeholder confidence, and drive overall efficiency in the banking sector.

items.title: An sEMG-Based Ergonomic Assessment of Mechanical Keyboard Switches: User Experience, Typing Performance and Bilateral Forearm Muscle Activation
items.abstract: Mechanical keyboard switches differ in force–travel characteristics, tactile feedback, and sound, but their combined effects on user experience, typing performance, and muscular loading remain unclear. We compared four switch types (Clicky, Tactile, Linear, and Silent) using subjective, performance, and surface electromyography (sEMG) measures. Twenty healthy, right-handed adults completed standardized typing tasks under all four conditions in a 4 × 4 balanced Latin square. Custom ratings, System Usability Scale, NASA Task Load Index, typing speed and accuracy, and bilateral forearm muscle activity normalized to maximum voluntary contraction were recorded. A Symmetry Index described side-to-side activation balance. Switch type significantly affected perceived noise, pleasure, and tactile feedback. Clicky switches received the highest pleasure and tactile-feedback ratings but the least favorable noise ratings, whereas Silent switches showed the opposite pattern. Silent switches also required more self-rated effort than Tactile switches. Typing speed, accuracy, usability, overall workload, and mean forearm muscle activity did not differ. The exploratory Symmetry Index showed clear side-to-side differences within individuals, but these did not differ across switch types. In this short typing task, switch design affected the subjective typing experience more than performance or muscular loading.

items.title: Antes do prompt: formulação de problemas e definição de objetivos no uso de inteligência artificial generativa por empreendedores
items.abstract: The diffusion of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) tools among entrepreneurs has been accompanied by a practical emphasis on writing prompts. This theoretical essay argues that this emphasis diverts attention from an earlier and more consequential step: formulating the problem and defining the outcome one seeks to achieve. We distinguish two patterns of use. In task-first use, the entrepreneur asks the AI for an immediate deliverable (a text, a plan, an analysis) without making explicit the goal it serves. In outcome-first use, the entrepreneur first states the desired outcome, diagnoses the problem, defines success criteria and constraints, and only then delegates tasks to the AI. We integrate four bodies of literature: research on problem finding and problem formulation, goal-setting theory, research on entrepreneurial decision-making under uncertainty (effectuation, the scientific approach, and experimentation), and recent empirical evidence on productivity, human–AI collaboration, and overreliance on automation. Building on this integration, we propose a conceptual model of pre-prompt problem formulation, with mechanisms (goal fit, calibrated evaluation, and selective implementation) and boundary conditions (task structure, position relative to the AI capability frontier, degree of uncertainty, and the entrepreneur's baseline performance), and we derive eight propositions. We discuss implications for individual entrepreneurs, limitations of the argument, and a research agenda that includes a three-arm field experiment. The article presents no empirical data; its propositions are intended for testing.

items.title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND INCLUSION: RETHINKING TEACHER EDUCATION
items.abstract: This theoretical article examines how artificial intelligence (AI) can contribute to teacher education in Francophone Africa in support of inclusive education. Drawing on a critical synthesis of academic literature and institutional frameworks, it analyses AI’s potential to support differentiated instruction, the transformation of teachers’ professional roles, and the ethical, linguistic and infrastructural challenges associated with its adoption. It proposes a four-dimensional teacher-education model comprising technological, pedagogical, ethical and contextual dimensions. AI can support the personalization of learning, provided that teachers retain professional responsibility and that inequalities of access, local languages and educational realities are taken into account. The proposed model offers a conceptual framework for critical and context-sensitive integration of AI and requires empirical validation.

items.title: Artificial intelligence based human resource analytics and sustainability driven employee job performance through the mediating role of employee engagement in the information technology sector
items.abstract: The use of Artificial Intelligence in Human Resource Management has changed how organizations analyse workforce information and support HR decision-making, creating new opportunities to strengthen sustainable employee performance. This study examines the relationship between Artificial Intelligence-Based Human Resource Analytics (AI-HRA) and Sustainability-Driven Employee Job Performance (SDEJP), while also investigating the mediating role of Employee Engagement among employees in the Information Technology industry. The study is primarily grounded in Job Demands-Resources (JD-R) Theory, while the Resource-Based View (RBV) provides a complementary perspective by viewing AI-HRA as an organizational capability. Data were collected from 350 IT employees, of whom 69.4% were male ( n = 243) and 30.6% were female ( n = 107), and analysed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS 3. The findings indicate significant positive relationships between AI-HRA and both Employee Engagement and SDEJP. Employee Engagement also has a significant positive relationship with SDEJP and partially mediates the relationship between AI-HRA and SDEJP. The measurement and structural models demonstrate acceptable levels of reliability, validity, predictive relevance, and model fit. The present research contributes to the growing body of evidence on artificial intelligence-enhanced human resource management by linking an organizational AI-HRA capability with employee-level engagement and sustainable job performance. In practice, the results emphasize the significance of adopting AI-based human resource analytics alongside employee engagement interventions for sustainable employee performance and interpreted as positive associations within the sampled context rather than as evidence that AI-HRA automatically improves employee outcomes.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence for the Verification of Nasogastric Tube Position in Chest Radiographs: A Systematic Review
items.abstract: Nasogastric tube (NGT) malposition is a significant patient-safety concern, and chest radiography is commonly used to confirm tube position before the tube is used.This systematic review evaluated the diagnostic performance and clinical usefulness of artificial intelligence (AI) systems in assessing NGT or related enteric feeding-tube position on radiographs.PubMed, Embase via Ovid, IEEE Xplore, and the National Health Service (NHS) Knowledge and Library Hub were searched from inception up to September 1, 2026, with additional backward and forward citation searching.Studies were included if they evaluated AIbased assessment of tube position on radiographs, and risk of bias and applicability were assessed using appropriate tools.A total of 131 records were identified, 32 duplicates were removed, and 99 records were screened.Nineteen reports were sought for retrieval, three could not be retrieved, 16 underwent full-text assessment, and 13 studies were included.Most studies were retrospective, and one was a prospective silent NHS validation.Task-specific AI models generally performed well in internal or development datasets, and some external studies reported area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) values above 0.90.However, performance was inconsistent across different hospitals and datasets, and several studies were limited by small numbers of unsafe tubes, class imbalance, selected patient groups, and the reuse of the same public datasets or related models.In the prospective NHS study, sensitivity for unsafe NGT position was 86.5% and negative predictive value (NPV) was 98%, although false-negative cases and AI processing failures still occurred.General-purpose multimodal large language models (LLMs) performed poorly, with sensitivity for abnormal NGT position ranging from 0% to 18.4%.Overall, AI may be useful for triage and clinical decision support, but current evidence does not support autonomous NGT verification.Further prospective, independent, multicentre studies in representative clinical populations are needed.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence in Breast Cancer Diagnosis, Treatment, and Perioperative Management: A Systematic Review of Current Applications and Future Perspectives.
items.abstract: Background: Breast cancer is the most frequently diagnosed malignancy in women globally, accounting for approximately 2.30 million new cases and 666,103 deaths in 2022. Artificial intelligence technologies including machine learning, deep learning, radiomics, and natural language processing have been widely applied across the breast cancer care continuum. However, no systematic review restricted to primary studies with patient-level or image-level data has synthesized evidence spanning all clinical domains simultaneously. Objectives: To evaluate the performance, methodological quality, and clinical relevance of artificial intelligence primary studies across screening and diagnostic imaging, digital pathology, radiomics, perioperative management, prognostic prediction, and natural language processing in breast cancer. Methods: PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched from January 2015 to May 2026. Eligibility was restricted to original primary research reporting patient-level or image-level data; secondary syntheses were explicitly excluded. Risk of bias was assessed using QUADAS-2 and PROBAST. Reporting followed PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Results: Of 5,275 identified records, 17 primary studies met eligibility criteria. In screening mammography (seven studies; n = 7,540 to 144,231 examinations), deep learning achieved area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) values of 0.876 to 0.939; a randomised trial in 80,033 women demonstrated non-inferiority to double reading with a 44.3% reduction in radiologist workload. In digital pathology (five studies; 270 to 44,732 whole-slide images), deep learning achieved AUC 0.985 to 0.994, exceeding unassisted pathologist performance in lymph node metastasis detection. Magnetic resonance imaging radiomics predicted pathological complete response in HER2-positive breast cancer with AUC 0.80. No breast cancer-specific perioperative primary study met the eligibility criteria. Deep survival networks achieved concordance index 0.626 versus 0.612 for Cox regression in breast cancer cohorts. Natural language processing identified metastatic recurrence in breast cancer clinical records with sensitivity 83% and specificity 73%. Risk of bias was low to moderate for imaging and pathology studies and high for small sample radiomics studies. Density-stratified performance was reported by only two imaging studies, and receptor status prediction from haematoxylin and eosin staining had not been validated as a safe alternative to immunohistochemistry. Conclusions: Artificial intelligence demonstrated clinically meaningful performance across the five domains with eligible primary studies. Breast cancer-specific perioperative and intensive care primary studies were absent, representing the largest evidence gap. External validation, demographic diversity, and prospective clinical integration evidence remained the most consistently identified limitations. Prediction of molecular receptor status without immunohistochemistry requires rigorous prospective safety validation before it can complement standard testing.

items.abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how artificial intelligence (AI) is implemented across marketing functions and analyses how the knowledge associated with AI is managed. It also explores how AI-related knowledge supports marketing decision-making and organizational learning while identifying future research lines for strengthening knowledge management (KM) practices in marketing contexts. Design/methodology/approach This study follows a two-stage research design. First, a systematic literature review is developed to identify and classify the main variables linking AI, marketing and KM. These variables are coded into a binary matrix and analyzed through multiple correspondence analysis under a homogeneity analysis by alternating least squares, implemented in R and Visual Studio Code. Findings AI adoption in marketing is primarily associated with four interconnected areas: customer-oriented personalization and behavioral response, KM foundations, strategic knowledge-based decision support and AI-enabled operational marketing applications. The analysis shows meaningful associations between AI use and customer knowledge, market knowledge, predictive analytics, personalization and strategic marketing capabilities. Originality/value This study contributes to the intersection of AI, marketing and KM by conceptualizing AI in marketing as a knowledge-based organizational mechanism rather than only as an operational technology. It shows how AI-related knowledge is integrated into marketing functions and decision-making processes, offering a structured mapping of the field and clarifying AI’s potential to support organizational learning and strategic marketing decisions.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence in Next-Generation Firewalls for Discriminating Cyber Attacks from Legitimate Service Traffic Surges
items.abstract: Next-generation firewalls (NGFWs) sit on the critical path between public networks and production services. Their most consequential error is no longer a missed signature; it is the inability to tell a malicious flood from a genuine surge in legitimate demand. Flash crowds, seasonal campaigns, media-driven spikes, and elastic microservice fan-out can resemble distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) traffic in volume while remaining economically and operationally valid. Static access-control lists, fixed rate limits, and signature catalogs therefore produce an unacceptable trade-off: either they under-block stealthy application-layer attacks or they over-block paying users. This article reviews, compares, and synthesizes peer-reviewed evidence from 2020 onward on machine-learning and deep-learning methods that can be embedded in NGFW and software-defined enforcement points to discriminate attacks from legitimate service-intensity bursts. We organize the literature into statistical filters, classical classifiers, representation-learning hybrids, sequential models, and two-tier designs that first cheaply detect a burst and then classify its intent. Published detectors regularly report accuracy above 98% on CICDDoS2019 and related traces, yet most benchmarks omit a dedicated flash-event class, which inflates apparent performance and leaves the operationally hardest decision under-tested. Building on that gap, we propose AID-NGFW, a three-tier architecture that couples entropy and cumulative-sum screening with a calibrated three-class discriminator (benign, flash crowd, attack) and a policy engine that drops malicious flows while scaling or shaping legitimate surges. Comparative tables and figures compile reported accuracies, F1-scores, datasets, and latency–accuracy trade-offs. We argue that the scientific and engineering priority is no longer binary attack detection in isolation, but reliable, low-latency, and explainable discrimination under encrypted traffic, class imbalance, concept drift, and adversarial mimicry.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Meets Cancer Immunology: Transforming Tumor Immune Microenvironment Analysis and Precision Immunotherapy
items.abstract: Cancer immunotherapy has fundamentally reshaped oncology by demonstrating that immune modulation can generate durable clinical responses in patients with advanced malignancies. However, the effectiveness of current immunotherapeutic approaches remains restricted by substantial interpatient variability, primary resistance, and acquired immune escape mechanisms. These limitations largely originate from the complexity of the tumor immune microenvironment (TIME), where malignant cells interact dynamically with heterogeneous immune populations, stromal components, metabolic networks, and molecular signaling pathways. Conventional biomarker approaches based on individual immune markers, such as PD-L1 expression or tumor mutational burden, provide incomplete predictions because they fail to capture the multidimensional nature of tumor immune interactions. Artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a transformative approach capable of integrating large-scale biological datasets generated through genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, single-cell sequencing, and spatial omics technologies. Machine learning, deep learning, and emerging foundation models provide unprecedented opportunities to decode immune ecosystems, identify novel biomarkers, predict immunotherapy responsiveness, and accelerate the development of personalized cancer treatments. Recent advances demonstrate that AI-driven models can characterize immune cell states, reconstruct spatial immune architectures, and improve patient stratification for immune checkpoint inhibitors. This review discusses the evolving intersection between AI and cancer immunology, focusing on how computational approaches are transforming TIME analysis, biomarker discovery, and precision immunotherapy. We critically evaluate current challenges, including algorithmic bias, model interpretability, clinical validation, and regulatory implementation. Finally, we highlight future directions toward AI-powered immuno-oncology platforms capable of integrating biological knowledge with computational intelligence to achieve individualized and more effective cancer therapies.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence-Driven Digital Twin for Disease Progression Prediction: A Comprehensive Review
items.abstract: Purpose: This study aims to integrate machine learning and deep learning techniques with Digital Twin technology to improve the accuracy of disease progression prediction and support personalised clinical decision-making. Design/Methodology/Approach: The study reviews existing Digital Twin frameworks in healthcare and proposes an Artificial Intelligence-driven Digital Twin paradigm based on temporal electronic health record data. The proposed approach develops dynamic digital representations of patients that reflect their current health conditions and predict their future clinical evolution. Machine learning and deep learning techniques analyse large-scale medical data, identify hidden patterns, and provide early predictions of patient deterioration, particularly in intensive care environments. Research Limitation: Further validation using diverse, multi-centre clinical datasets and real-time patient information is required before the model can be widely implemented in clinical practice. Findings: The findings indicate that AI-powered Digital Twins can improve the accuracy of disease progression prediction, facilitate early identification of patient deterioration, and support clinical treatment decisions. The proposed approach may also enable proactive, personalised, and data-driven disease management. Practical Implication: The proposed Digital Twin paradigm can help healthcare professionals monitor patients, identify high-risk cases, select appropriate interventions, and allocate critical care resources more effectively. Social Implication: Improved early prediction and personalised treatment may reduce mortality rates, prevent avoidable complications, enhance healthcare quality, and reduce the clinical and economic burden on patients and healthcare institutions. Originality/Value: This study highlights the value of combining temporal electronic health record data, Artificial Intelligence, and Digital Twin technology within a unified framework for predicting disease progression. It contributes to the development of intelligent and patient-specific clinical decision-support systems for critical healthcare environments.

items.title: Artificial intelligence-enabled bioprinting for tumor modeling: from biomimetic microenvironment reconstruction to drug screening
items.abstract: Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) and three-dimensional (3D) bioprinting have provided new strategies for developing in vitro tumor models with improved representation of native tumor microenvironments. This review examines the role of AI across the entire bioprinting workflow—from image-based model design and real-time printing control to post-printing functional assessment and high-throughput drug evaluation. We first outline how machine learning and deep learning algorithms optimize bioink formulation, predict the mechanical behavior of printed constructs, and enable error correction during fabrication. We then discuss AI-driven strategies for reconstructing key components of the tumor microenvironment, including extracellular matrices with tunable mechanical properties, perfusable vascular networks, and spatially organized multi-cellular architectures that incorporate cancer cells, stromal cells, and immune populations. The review further addresses the application of AI-enhanced bioprinted tumor models in automated drug screening, resistance mechanism studies, and personalized medicine, with particular attention to the integration of patient-derived cells and multi-omics data. We also evaluate current challenges, including the trade-off between biomimetic fidelity and throughput, the lack of standardized protocols and data repositories, and the need for improved model validation against clinical outcomes. Finally, we discuss emerging directions such as closed-loop optimization systems, intelligent bioinks, and the integration of bioprinting with organ-on-a-chip platforms. By providing a comprehensive overview of this rapidly evolving field, this review aims to inform researchers and clinicians about the current capabilities and future potential of AI-assisted bioprinted tumor models for oncology research and therapeutic development.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence-enhanced Blockchain Telehealth Systems: Pioneering Secure and Intelligent Remote Healthcare Delivery
items.abstract: The artificial intelligence (AI)-enhanced Blockchain telehealth framework proposes a new architecture that addresses remote healthcare delivery challenges through AI and Blockchain technologies, making services secure, intelligent, and transparent. Traditional telehealth delivery models face significant data security, privacy, and trust concerns. This study addresses these issues by applying AI predictive analytics to assess service delivery risk among patient populations through patterns of telehealth utilization and accessibility across demographic, ethnic, and geographic cohorts. After collecting and preprocessing patient information from the Telehealth Services for Medicaid and CHIP Population dataset, a Gradient Boosting Machine model was developed, achieving 99.96 percent accuracy, 99.89 percent precision, 99.98 percent recall, and a 99.93 percent F1-score. The experimental evaluation showed promising performance, with very low gas consumption of about 22,500 units per transaction, a latency of 0.013 seconds, and a strong encryption throughput of 57.75 MB/s. These results confirm that the framework is scalable and highly efficient. Overall, the proposed framework would improve security, reliability, and interoperability in the telehealth ecosystem, supporting more robust, resilient, and patient-centered sustainable digital health initiatives.

items.title: Association of generative artificial intelligence use with perceived academic benefit and reported performance among medical students
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) tools are widely adopted by medical students. Although student attitudes toward AI have been surveyed extensively, far less is known about whether students who use these tools more often also report better academic outcomes. This study asked whether AI usage frequency is associated with perceived academic benefit and with self-reported academic performance among medical students at a single institution. A cross-sectional survey was administered to medical students at a single U.S. allopathic medical school. Students reported AI usage frequency, perceived academic benefit (composite of three Likert-scale items; Cronbach’s α = 0.84), self-reported overall exam performance, and self-rated academic standing. Spearman correlations with 95% confidence intervals and Kruskal-Wallis tests were used to examine associations. Of 103 respondents, students who used AI more frequently reported significantly greater perceived academic benefit (ρ = 0.69, 95% CI [0.57, 0.78], P < 0.001). However, AI usage frequency was not correlated with self-reported exam performance (ρ = −0.02, P = 0.81) or self-rated academic standing (ρ = −0.01, P = 0.93). Over half of students (53.4%) reported using AI Often or Always for studying. In this exploratory single-institution study, students who used AI more frequently perceived greater academic benefit, but this perception was not reflected in coarse, self-reported performance measures. This discrepancy should be interpreted cautiously and is at least as likely to reflect a measurement artifact, arising from the insensitivity of a single global performance item, recall bias, and the inability to distinguish performance before and after AI adoption, as a true gap between perception and attainment. Findings underscore the importance of helping medical students critically evaluate their AI-assisted study practices and identify priorities for more rigorous future investigation using objective, granular performance outcomes.

items.abstract: This research and policy paper, authored by Daniel Robert Izzo, proposes establishing an international extraterrestrial mineral reserve based on the metal-rich asteroid (16) Psyche, with the long-term objective of allocating up to $1 billion in potential future mineral value to every person on Earth and helping eliminate global poverty. The proposal examines the asteroid's estimated mineral resources, NASA's Psyche mission, robotic mining technologies, and the potential establishment of a lunar mineral depository for the storage, verification, and management of extraterrestrial resources. The paper also documents the author's historical proposals concerning the self-ownership and incorporation of Asteroid 16 Psyche, its proposed association with Marie Byrd Land and Ellsworth Land in Antarctica, and a trust framework intended to benefit humanity through potential cooperation with the United States and United Nations. These arrangements are presented as proposals and author-reported historical actions, not as internationally recognized territorial or property rights. Additional subjects include international space law, economic feasibility, the proposed financing of future space infrastructure, equitable distribution of resource proceeds, and scientific milestones necessary to evaluate the concept. The $1 billion per-person allocation is a speculative long-term policy objective, not an existing financial asset, guaranteed payment, or currently redeemable entitlement. Implementation would require substantial technological advances, independently verified resource valuations, and lawful international governance. items.title: Attacking visual foundation depth estimation model with adaptable adversarial patch
items.abstract: Vision foundation models (VFMs) have demonstrated strong generalization ability across various downstream tasks and scenes. However, their vulnerability to adversarial examples, particularly in safety-critical applications, remains insufficiently understood. This paper investigates the attack effect of physical adversarial patches on monocular depth estimation (MDE) models, specifically the foundation model Depth Anything, widely used in fields such as autonomous driving and robotic navigation. First, we introduce a universal patch attack pipeline and present the following key observations: 1) Attack effectiveness : In the pixel-wise dense prediction task of MDE, adversarial effects are largely confined to the patch area and do not spread to other regions, indicating that foundation models have enhanced adversarial robustness compared to traditional models. 2) Attack interpretability : The learned adversarial patches often contain semantically meaningful content, such as forests or buildings, leading to corresponding erroneous depth predictions, which adds interpretability to the attack’s behavior. Based on the observations, we focus on improving the applicability of adversarial patches in real-world environments by proposing a plug-and-play augmentation method, termed MixCrop, that enhances attack effectiveness, especially when patch semantics are incomplete or repetitive. Extensive experiments including physical attacks demonstrate that the patched objects can effectively vanish from the predicted depth map. The learned patches also have strong generalization ability across various objects and scenes.

items.title: AURA - AI POWERED ADAPTIVE LEARNING
items.abstract: Most online courses give every learner the same lessons at the same pace, so gaps in understanding often go unnoticed. This presents AURA (AI-Powered Adaptive Learning System), a web application that generates a course from a learner’s goal and adapts it to the learner’s quiz results. A large language model (LLM) creates a course outline with modules, lessons, topics and prerequisite links, and each lesson is written when the learner opens it. A tutor based on retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) answers questions from the current lesson and cites the passages it used. After each multiple-choice quiz, a weighted moving average updates a mastery score and a confidence value for the topic, and fixed rules select the next step and the next quiz difficulty. All LLM output is validated against schemas. In a pilot run with the gpt-5.4-mini model, five of seven generation jobs succeeded on the first attempt without repair. Two failed, one because of a provider quota error and one because the safety-check output was invalid. A course outline and first lesson were ready in 26.6 s. The prototype supports multiple-choice questions only, uses fixed adaptation rules and has not been tested with real learners.

items.title: Automated Confirmation Bias-Epistemic Laundering and Sycophancy in Statutory AI Decision-Making
items.abstract: Recent operational deployments of Large Language Models (LLMs) within public safety and statutory decision-making frameworks—highlighted by active misconduct investigations into police deployment of generative AI—expose a critical vulnerability in information governance and data integrity. This paper formalises the concept of "epistemic laundering": the mechanism by which Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) optimisation creates structural sycophancy, causing LLMs to extract subtle, unconscious human bias and transform it into authoritative institutional record. When deployed in decision-justification, risk-assessment, or investigative roles, these systems do not provide objective analytical rigour; instead, they function as automated confirmation engines that corrupt the evidentiary record. By disarming human critical verification through fluent, polished output, sycophantic models induce severe automation bias, leading to the total breakdown of information governance controls and human-in-the-loop verification. Applying formal information management principles, this paper evaluates these failure modes and proposes strict domain boundaries and record-keeping protocols to protect statutory data integrity. Keywords: Epistemic laundering, large language models, reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF), sycophancy, information governance, statutory decision-making, audit boundary, automation bias.

items.title: Backdoor Attacks Against Cloud-Based Ai-As-A-Service: Stealthy Trigger Engineering and Detection
items.abstract: Cloud-based Artificial Intelligence-as-a-Service (AIaaS) enables the seamless deployment of custom machine learning models, yet introduces severe security risks. Malicious actors frequently upload backdoored models that function normally but execute targeted errors upon encountering a secret trigger. Most current backdoor attacks rely on visible triggers, such as image patches or specific text phrases, which are easily detected by cloud security systems. Furthermore, cloud platforms automatically process uploaded data such as compressing images or tokenizing text before analysis, a mechanism that traditional attacks and defenses frequently overlook. This paper presents a novel framework that exploits and defends against these automated data processing pipelines. An attack technique that relies on the notion of pre-processing synthesis to hide the presence of the trigger, referred to as Preprocessing-Synthesized Triggers, is presented herein. In this technique, the hidden trigger is not present in the initially uploaded data set but rather in the manner in which the artificial intelligence has been trained to react after the cloud service applies data transformation, such as compression and resizing of the data set. For cloud providers, a new mechanism for detecting these hidden triggers is also developed under the name of Differential Pipeline Activation Analysis (DPAA). The idea here is to detect malicious activation of the AI system by applying small changes to its data processing pipeline within the cloud environment. Large variation in the response of the AI’s internal logic indicates possible attacks on the system. According to experimental results, this new attack can effectively evade conventional backdoor attacks as no statistical anomalies are observable in the raw data set, whereas the new defense can detect these triggers successfully at more than 95 percent accuracy.

items.title: Bayesian hierarchical downscaling of station observations with learned covariance kernels: an artificial intelligence evaluation of uncertainty propagation in national climate normals
items.abstract: National climate normals are typically reported as single numbers, yet they inherit uncertainty from sparse station networks, interpolation choices and covariance assumptions. The framework is applied to NASA POWER monthly reanalysis air temperature at 2 m for Lagos, Nigeria (6.52°N, 3.38°E) over 2000–2023, comprising 312 monthly observations with a mean of 26.414 °C and a standard deviation of 0.943 °C. The warming trend is estimated at 0.1553 °C per decade. A hierarchical model with a Matérn covariance whose smoothness and length-scale are inferred from the data is compared against fixed-kernel alternatives, and the resulting posterior predictive variance is decomposed into components attributable to the kernel, the trend and the residual. Kernel learning changes the width of the 95% credible band for annual means by a non-trivial margin and that fixed-kernel downscaling systematically under-reports uncertainty at the decadal scale. The contribution is a formal propagation model that makes the kernel a first-class inferential object, together with a diagnostic that flags when national normals are reported with false precision.

items.title: Between Cairo and Cape Town: Architectural Education, Decolonisation and the Question of Architectural Intelligence
items.abstract: This perspective article asks whether architectural education can deliver the transformation it declares, and what that question becomes once artificial intelligence (AI) enters the studio. The article distils two 2026 keynotes delivered by the author, in Cairo and Cape Town, and reads them against the UIA Global Survey of 345 schools in 159 countries and recent work on decolonised pedagogy and algorithmic colonialism. The findings demonstrate that schools converge on accreditation, studio learning and sustainability but diverge significantly on agendas requiring serious and committed change, with decolonised pedagogy in only 29% of programmes. Because AI learns from the archives and canons decolonial pedagogy seeks to open, this implementation gap presents the challenge of being automated, with Euro-American forms returning as statistical defaults. The key contribution is that this article links institutional evidence to epistemic critique and distinguishes artificial from architectural intelligence, calling for situated, embodied, cultural and relational judgement. The limitation is that this is an argued position based on published evidence and does not present new empirical testing. Yet the article outlines responses including comparative prompting, absence mapping, bias auditing and community-governed datasets.
